industry_radar.thesis: Agents moving from assistive features toward production workflows, ARR and measurable usage.
More autonomous agents expand identity, permission, runtime and governance attack surfaces.
AI-driven product discovery is beginning to create measurable commerce traffic/conversion.
Hyperscaler custom accelerators diversify spend beyond merchant GPUs.
AI memory demand remains supply-constrained with multi-year capacity buildout.
Scale-out cluster bandwidth/power constraints shift value toward networking and optical components.
AI inference expands into low-power edge devices; early company-level demand inflections visible.
Grid connection, transformers, switchgear, generation and cooling remain key physical bottlenecks.
Hyperscalers increasingly pursue on-site generation/storage where grid interconnection is slow.
New enrichment capacity and government-backed domestic fuel-chain investment are moving toward commercial scale.
Fiber, building systems, power solutions and interconnection backlogs remain strong.
Domestic capex and labor economics support automation, but not all robotics subthemes are commercially mature.
US drone/autonomy demand is constrained by domestic production and component capacity.
Bookings/backlogs at defense electronics and component suppliers show strong program demand.
Launch capacity and sovereign-access bottlenecks support alternative launch and space-system suppliers.
Satellite spectrum and terrestrial-mobile integration are becoming strategic telecom infrastructure.
Oral, pediatric and geographic expansion broaden obesity treatment beyond first-generation injections.
Robotic surgery, PFA and specialty device platforms expand penetration; competition also rising.
More pharma companies are licensing AI research platforms, but clinical validation remains the hard gate.
Stablecoins are becoming regulated payment/settlement infrastructure with rapid on-chain volume growth.
Event contracts, tokenization and always-on markets are moving from niche products toward market structure.
Paid services and city expansion show autonomous ride-hailing moving beyond pilot phase.
Aircraft deliveries/orderbooks remain strong, supporting component suppliers with scarce capacity.
Policy and supply-chain security drive US-aligned rare-earth and critical-material capacity.
Grid, data center and electrification demand meets constrained mine supply.
Advanced materials see broad demand across semis, defense, space, power and telecom.
